lesson.title: Build AI Customer Support Agents Across Three Platforms

sources.title: Build AI Customer Support Agents Across Three Platforms

steps.title: Create OpenAI FAQ Support Agent
steps.instructions: Open OpenAI Agent Builder, create a new workflow, drag an Agent block onto the canvas, and name it (e.g. FAQ Support Agent). Ask ChatGPT for a Markdown support prompt and paste it into the Instructions field.

targets.caption: Drag an Agent block from the Core panel onto the canvas
Paste the ChatGPT-generated Markdown prompt into Instructions

explanations.topic: Agent Builder canvas and node categories
Using ChatGPT to generate structured Markdown prompts

hints: Open the Agents section in the left sidebar of the OpenAI Platform and click Open Agent Builder.
Connect the Start block to your new Agent block and rename it in the right-hand settings panel.
Ask ChatGPT for a single-block Markdown prompt with a Role Definition and 3 User message / Agent response examples, then paste it into Instructions.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to connect the Start node to the Agent block on the canvas.
Writing vague instructions instead of including role boundaries and example responses.
steps.code: I'm building a customer support agent for a SaaS company using OpenAI Agents Builder. The agent needs to answer questions about features, pricing, and billing

steps.title: Attach PDF and test OpenAI agent
steps.instructions: Click the plus icon next to Tools, select File search, and upload your product documentation PDF. Click Preview to test a pricing question, then click Publish to create a production version.

targets.caption: Click + in Tools and choose File search to upload your PDF
Open Preview at the top of the canvas to chat with the agent

explanations.topic: OpenAI Agent Builder limitations and MCP connectors

hints: Click the + icon in the Tools row of the Agent settings panel.
Choose File search, upload your PDF, wait for indexing to finish, and click Attach.
Use the play-shaped Preview button at the top to ask a question from your PDF, then click Publish.
common_mistakes: Closing the upload modal before clicking Attach after the PDF finishes uploading.
Testing before the vector store has finished processing.

steps.title: Set up Botpress bot and knowledge
steps.instructions: Sign in to Botpress, click Create Bot, and complete the 4-step wizard with your bot name, Customer Support goal, website URL, and product PDF. Once Botpress Studio opens, rename the default AutonomousNode to Main_Support_Agent.

targets.caption: Start a new bot from your Botpress workspace
Verify the Autonomous Node can query your Knowledge Base

explanations.topic: How Botpress Autonomous Nodes reason dynamically
How Botpress RAG retrieves relevant chunks

hints: Click + Create Bot in the Botpress dashboard to launch the setup wizard.
Select Customer Support as the goal, provide your website URL for personality, and upload your PDF in step 4.
Click Train agent, continue into Botpress Studio, and click the AutonomousNode title to rename it Main_Support_Agent.
common_mistakes: Skipping the Knowledge upload step in the wizard and leaving the bot without product context.
Leaving the node name generic instead of naming it clearly before adding transitions.

steps.title: Connect WhatsApp and test Botpress emulator
steps.instructions: Open Explore Hub in the integrations panel to browse or connect channels like WhatsApp and inspect per-node LLM options under Advanced settings. Open the Emulator tab on the right and test knowledge-base questions.

targets.caption: Open Botpress Hub to install WhatsApp or other integrations
Switch to the Emulator tab to test live responses

explanations.topic: Per-node LLM model selection and zero token markup

hints: Use the left sidebar integrations icon and click Find more on the Hub to locate WhatsApp.
Click the Emulator tab in the top-right panel of Botpress Studio.
Send a greeting or ask about trials and cancellation to confirm answers come from your Knowledge Base.
common_mistakes: Inspecting the Inspector tab instead of switching to the Emulator tab to chat.
Forgetting to enable or index knowledge sources in Knowledge Bases before testing.

steps.title: Create Zapier AI agent with prompt
steps.instructions: Go to Agents in Zapier, click New agent, and choose Start from scratch. Ask ChatGPT for a Zapier-optimized prompt that handles FAQs and demo lead capture, then paste it into Copilot's Describe your workflow field.

targets.caption: Paste the Zapier-optimized ChatGPT prompt into Copilot
Review the instructions generated by Zapier Copilot

explanations.topic: Zapier Agents as action-first automation engines

hints: Select Agents (Beta) in Zapier's left navigation bar and click + New agent.
Pick Start from scratch so Copilot prompts you to describe your workflow.
Generate an action-oriented Markdown prompt in ChatGPT mentioning Google Sheets demo capture, paste it in, and click Start building.
common_mistakes: Using a generic chatbot prompt that does not tell Zapier when to switch into lead-capture mode.
Confusing Copilot's setup chat on the left with the live user test preview.
steps.code: I'm building an AI agent in Zapier that: Answers customer questions about pricing and features, Detects when a user wants to request a demo

steps.title: Add Zapier knowledge, Sheets, and test
steps.instructions: Click Add knowledge source to upload your product PDF, then click Add tool to attach Google Sheets Create Spreadsheet Row. Add an On demand trigger and test booking a demo in the agent chat.

targets.caption: Choose Upload File to attach your product PDF
Set the Trigger to On demand before testing

hints: Scroll down the Configure pane to Knowledge sources and upload your PDF.
Under Tools this agent can use, click + Add tool, search Google Sheets, and select Create Spreadsheet Row.
Click Add a trigger to start the agent, choose On demand, and reply with a demo request to verify the Sheets action runs.
common_mistakes: Trying to test the Zapier agent before adding an On demand trigger.
Selecting a Google Sheets spreadsheet that lacks column headers when running Create Spreadsheet Row.

steps.title: Build Botpress lead capture and table
steps.instructions: In Botpress Studio, add a Standard Node named Collect_Lead_Info with Person Name and Email Address cards stored in workflow.lead_name and workflow.lead_email. Create a LeadsTable with Name and Email columns, then add an Insert Record card mapping those variables.

targets.caption: Add Person Name, Email Address, and Insert Record cards
Create a table with Name and Email columns

hints: Right-click the canvas in Botpress Studio to add a Standard Node and rename it Collect_Lead_Info.
Add Person Name and Email Address cards and create variables named lead_name and lead_email in Store result in.
Open Tables in the left sidebar, create LeadsTable with Name and Email columns, then add an Insert Record card referencing {{workflow.lead_name}} and {{workflow.lead_email}}.
common_mistakes: Placing the Insert Record card above the name and email capture cards instead of after them.
Forgetting to create the Name and Email columns in LeadsTable before configuring Insert Record.

steps.title: Add transition condition and test leads
steps.instructions: Add a Transition card to Main_Support_Agent with the condition event.preview?.toLowerCase().includes('demo') and wire it to Collect_Lead_Info and End. Test typing demo in the Emulator and verify the saved row in LeadsTable.

targets.caption: Enter the JavaScript condition in the Transition card
Send demo in the Emulator to trigger lead capture

hints: Click + Add Card on Main_Support_Agent and search for Transition under Flow Logic.
Paste event.preview?.toLowerCase().includes('demo') into the Condition field and drag a connector from that card to Collect_Lead_Info.
Connect Collect_Lead_Info to End, test 'demo' in the Emulator, and check LeadsTable in the Tables tab.
common_mistakes: Leaving the Transition card disconnected from Collect_Lead_Info.
Omitting ?. or .toLowerCase() in the Condition expression.

steps.title: Publish and configure Botpress Webchat
steps.instructions: Click Publish and Publish changes to make your Botpress agent live. Open Webchat Deploy Settings to copy the website embed script tags, and customize Display Name and Bot Description under Bot Identity.

checks.label: Publish your updated workflow to deploy

targets.caption: Publish your updated workflow to deploy Webchat
Copy the script tags to embed the chat widget

explanations.topic: Monitoring conversations, users, and LLM analytics
Production checklist: cost, autonomous nodes, RAG, and deployment

hints: Use the Publish button in the top-right corner of Botpress Studio and confirm Publish changes.
Navigate to Webchat -> Deploy Settings in the dashboard sidebar to view the embed script tags.
Open Webchat -> Bot Identity to update the Display Name and description shown in the widget header.
common_mistakes: Editing the workflow after publishing without clicking Publish changes again.
Copying only one of the two script tags from Deploy Settings.
